en.name: Terrine
en.summary: An uncut terrine still sealed under its layer of fat or aspic keeps to the date on it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and a home-made one should be eaten within about a week. Cut it and it is a cooked meat dish: 3–4 days, or 1–2 months frozen at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: However rustic the earthenware dish looks, a terrine is a cooked, moist, low-acid, ready-to-eat meat and it lives in the refrigerator. Refrigerated pâtés and meat spreads are named as a Listeria risk, and Listeria grows at fridge temperature. The traditional practice of maturing a terrine for two or three days before cutting is about flavour, and it is done in the refrigerator, not in a larder. Out of the fridge give it two hours at most, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Uncut and sealed under its fat or aspic, keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and go by the date on it; a home-made one should be pressed, sealed and eaten within about a week. There is no separate general figure for the sealed state, because the seal is what is doing the work. Once you cut it, it is a cooked meat dish and keeps 3–4 days: press cling film directly onto the cut face so it does not grey, and keep the remaining fat or jelly layer over the rest. A liver terrine will darken at the cut face within hours — that is oxidation, not spoilage.
en.freezer: 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze it whole or in thick slabs rather than in slices, wrapped tightly in cling film and then foil. Aspic does not survive freezing and will weep out as a puddle on thawing, so a terrine set in jelly is a poorer candidate than one sealed with fat. Freeze it early rather than at the end of the cut window, and thaw it slowly so the texture holds.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight, or longer for a whole terrine, and use it within the cut window. Never thaw it on the counter, and do not refreeze.
spoilage: A sour, sharp or ammonia-like smell rather than a rich meaty one.
A slimy or tacky film on the cut face.
Grey-green patches beyond the normal darkening of exposed liver.
Mould anywhere on the surface, or fat that smells rancid.
tips: Press cling film onto the cut face; darkening there is oxidation, not spoilage.
Keep the fat or jelly layer intact over the uncut portion.
Freeze in thick slabs, never in slices.
Pregnant people should choose canned or shelf-stable meat spreads instead.

faq.q: How long does a terrine keep once cut?
faq.a: 3–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, with cling film pressed onto the cut face.

faq.q: How long does an uncut terrine keep?
faq.a: Follow the date on a bought one. A home-made terrine, pressed and sealed under fat, should be eaten within about a week, refrigerated.
Yes, 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F), in thick slabs. Aspic does not survive freezing and will weep out on thawing.

zh.name: 法式肉凍（terrine）
zh.summary: 尚未切開、仍被油脂或肉凍封住的 terrine，放 4 °C 以下並以其日期為準；自製的則應在大約一週內吃完。一旦切開，它就是一道熟肉料理：3～4 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 1～2 個月。
zh.pantry: 不管那個陶皿看起來多有鄉村氣息，terrine 都是煮熟、含水、低酸性的即食肉品，它住冰箱。冷藏的肝醬與肉類抹醬被點名為李斯特菌風險食品，而李斯特菌在冰箱溫度下就會生長。傳統上把 terrine 熟成兩三天再切，那是為了風味，而且是在冷藏中進行，不是放在儲藏室。離開冰箱最多兩小時，氣溫超過 32 °C 時最多一小時。
zh.fridge: 未切開、被油脂或肉凍封住時，請放 4 °C 以下並依其標示日期；自製的請壓實、封好，並在大約一週內吃完。未切開的狀態沒有另外的通用數字，因為真正在工作的是那層封。一旦切開，它就是熟肉料理，可放 3～4 天：把保鮮膜直接壓在切面上避免發灰，其餘部分則讓油脂或肉凍層繼續覆蓋。含肝的 terrine 切面幾小時內就會變深——那是氧化，不是腐敗。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 1～2 個月。請整條或切成厚塊冷凍，不要切片，並用保鮮膜緊包後再包鋁箔。肉凍（aspic）撐不過冷凍，解凍時會滲成一灘水，所以用肉凍定型的 terrine 比用油脂封的更不適合冷凍。請盡早冷凍，不要拖到切開後期限的尾端；解凍也要慢，質地才保得住。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍（整條要更久），並在切開後的期限內用完。不要放室溫退冰，也不要二次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸、刺鼻或有氨味，而不是濃郁的肉香。
切面出現黏滑或發黏的薄膜。
出現超過「肝暴露後正常變深」程度的灰綠色。
表面任何地方長霉，或油脂發出油耗味。
tips: 切面壓上保鮮膜；那裡變深是氧化不是腐敗。
未切的部分讓油脂或肉凍層保持完整。
冷凍時切厚塊，絕對不要切片。
孕婦請改選罐裝或常溫保存的肉類抹醬。

faq.q: terrine 切開後可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下 3～4 天，並在切面壓上保鮮膜。

faq.q: 還沒切開的可以放多久？
faq.a: 市售的依其標示日期。自製、壓實並以油脂封好的，冷藏下大約一週內吃完。
可以，−18 °C 下 1～2 個月，切厚塊冷凍。肉凍撐不過冷凍，解凍時會滲出來。
